title: Practitioners reject LLM-generated confidence scores as a decision basis
source_title: Using LLM for confidence scoring is a bad idea
summary: A blog post argues that using an LLM to produce confidence scores is a bad idea, drawing a large practitioner discussion about reliance on model-reported certainty.

title: Write-up advises against asking a model to state its own confidence
source_title: Don't ask an LLM for a confidence score
summary: A practitioner article argues that asking an LLM for a confidence score is not a reliable practice, adding to a series of reports that self-reported confidence from models is untrustworthy.

title: Teams struggle to fit non-deterministic AI outputs into conventional software
source_title: How to wrangle non-deterministic AI outputs into conventional software? (2025)
summary: An article asks how non-deterministic AI outputs can be wrangled into conventional software, framing determinism of model behaviour as a core integration obstacle.

title: Deterministic model inference alone did not make the surrounding pipeline deterministic
source_title: Deterministic LLM Inference Did Not Make Our Pipeline Deterministic
summary: A research note reports that a deterministic LLM inference setup did not result in a deterministic pipeline, a concrete case of residual non-determinism around the model call.

title: Early 2023 warning against asking LLMs to generate confidence scores
source_title: Never ask an LLM to generate a confidence score
summary: A 2023 blog post argues against asking an LLM to generate a confidence score, an early public report of unreliable model-stated certainty.

title: LLM confidence is often uncalibrated and resists standard calibration methods
source_title: Calibrating Large Language Models with Sample Consistency
quote: However, LLMs are often uncalibrated inherently and elude conventional calibration techniques due to their proprietary nature and massive scale.
summary: The paper notes that LLMs are often inherently uncalibrated and do not respond well to conventional calibration techniques, then evaluates deriving confidence from consistency across multiple sampled generations.

title: Calibrating LLM confidence via an auxiliary model trained on input and output text alone
source_title: Calibrating Large Language Models Using Their Generations Only
quote: However, finding effective ways to calibrate LLMs - especially when the only interface to the models is their generated text - remains a challenge.
summary: Proposes APRICOT, which trains an auxiliary model to predict an LLM's confidence from its textual input and output, motivated by the difficulty of calibrating confidence when only generated text is available.

title: Calibration methods miss that true confidence should reflect stability under distraction
source_title: CaliDist: Calibrating Large Language Models via Behavioral Robustness to Distraction
quote: In this paper, we argue that a model's true confidence should reflect its stability under cognitive pressure.
summary: Argues that calibration work overlooks behavioural robustness: a model's confidence should reflect how stable its predictions are when the prompt is perturbed with semantic distractors, and uses that stability signal to rescale confidence.

title: Open-ended generation exposes a semantic calibration gap in LLM confidence
source_title: S-EDL: Eliciting Self-Evidence from Sequence Likelihoods for Semantic Calibration of LLMs
quote: Calibrating large language models (LLMs) in open-ended generation is uniquely challenging because many distinct token sequences can express the same underlying meaning.
summary: Notes that calibration in open-ended generation is hard because many distinct token sequences express the same meaning, and proposes an evidential method that calibrates over prompt-specific semantic classes.

title: Binary question answering exposes poorly calibrated LLM token probabilities
source_title: Calibrated Large Language Models for Binary Question Answering
quote: A well-calibrated model should produce probabilities that accurately reflect the likelihood of its predictions being correct.
summary: Frames calibration as the alignment between predicted probabilities and actual correctness, then applies an inductive Venn-Abers predictor to the output-token probabilities of binary answers, reporting gains over temperature scaling on BoolQ with Llama 2.

title: Reproducible inference required a dedicated deterministic-operations patch
source_title: [Proof of Concept] Made vllm deterministic (tested for qwen3-8B)
summary: vLLM proof-of-concept pull request showed how to obtain fully deterministic inference in vLLM; the need for such a patch indicates batch-invariant reproducible output was not the default behavior.
notes: GitHub pull request; state=closed at collection time; metrics from unauthenticated search API.

title: Non-deterministic output reported at temperature zero without prefix caching
source_title: [Bug]: KV block corruption in base scheduler, Non-deterministic output at temperature=0 without prefix caching
summary: vLLM bug report: output was non-deterministic at temperature=0 without prefix caching, attributed by the reporter to KV block corruption in the base scheduler.
notes: GitHub issue state=open at collection time; metrics from unauthenticated search API.
